To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in the absence or removal of the presynaptic elements, the presynaptic sites can develop de novo on the dendrites of postsynaptic neurons in the adult brain.

the presynaptic dendrite is a normal morphological structure in adult mammalian CNS and that the de novo formation of synapses on these presynaptic dendritic sites is the main mechanism of the reactive synaptogenetic response in the cerebellum and in the lateral geniculate nucleus of adult rats and mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the morphological aspects of synaptic rearrangement in the adult central nervous system.
the morphological aspects of the plastic changes in adult mammalian CNS following deafferentation.
the morphological and functional plasticity of the nervous system, in particular with the mechanisms of synaptic reorganization in adult brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presynaptic dendritic sites are not only capable of receiving synaptic contacts but also of forming them.

the presynaptic dendritic sites in the cerebellum and LGN represent a new type of synapses, formed by the de novo formation of presynaptic sites by the dendritic processes of Golgi and granule cells and geniculo-corti- cal relay cells, respectively.
de novo" formation of presynaptic sites is a common feature in the adult brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the "de novo" formation of presynaptic dendritic sites by the Golgi cells of the cerebelar cortex and the geniculo-corticals relay cells of the LGN, is an example of the remarkable plasticity of the adult mammalian brain.

in the absence, in the adult mammalian brain, of axonal sprouts, the reactive synapse formation is achieved by the participation of newly formed presynaptic sites of dendritic origin, which are located in the vicinity of the pre-existing synapses of the dendrites.
de novo" presynaptic dendritic formation in adult mammalian CNS is a normal and not an abnormal phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in the adult brain, presynaptic dendritic growth is a normal and physiologically relevant process that may contribute to the formation of new synapses in response to injury or other pathological conditions.

the formation of presynaptic sites is a normal process in adult CNS and that the formation of synapses on the dendrites of the postsynaptic neurons is not restricted to the embryonic and early postnatal stages of development.

the presynaptic dendritic sites are formed in response to the need for synaptic transmission in a particular neuronal network, i.e. the new synapses are formed "de novo", and not as a result of the sprouting of the axons from the existing synapses.
